F01.question: I området Recursive self-improvement, vad är de två senaste nyheterna och vad handlar de om?
F01.answer:
The two latest papers on Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) are [31] and [32], both published on 2026-09-16.

[31] introduces ScienceBuddy, an interactive scientific research workspace that implements "recursive-in-recursive self-improvement" - a paradigm that couples harness evolution with model reinforcement learning. In this framework, the inner recursion improves the harness while keeping the model fixed, while the outer recursion trains the model under the improved harness. This allows harness evolution to shape training experience and creates new opportunities for harness adaptation as model learning progresses [31].

[32] proposes ModularRSI, a benchmark-disjoint, contrastive, and modular framework for generalizable harness evolution. ModularRSI contrasts successful and failed trajectories for the same task, aggregates evidence across tasks to identify recurring behavioral deficiencies, and decomposes the evolvable harness into five functional modules (Agent Loop, Tool Use, Observation Management, Context Management, and Task Completion Detection). Each module evolves independently within a restricted modification scope before being integrated into a unified harness [32].

F02.question: Vad har hänt med GUI agents den senaste månaden?
F02.answer:
In the last month, significant advancements have been made in GUI agent technology, with multiple new models and frameworks emerging. UI-Mate-27B has set a new open-weight state of the art on general computer-use benchmarks, scoring 77.0% on OSWorld-Verified and 66.2% on WindowsAgentArena [20]. The UI-Mate system integrates an environment-grounded training stack with in-context demonstration learning, which substantially improves long-horizon reliability as demonstrated by a single demonstration raising strict success from 17.2% to 35.4% on the 33-task self-demo subset [20].

LLaDA-UI, a 16.7B-parameter MoE-based, block-wise diffusion vision-language GUI agent, has been introduced, following a two-stage training pipeline that outperforms Qwen2.5-VL-7B and surpasses Qwen3-VL-8B on four of six reported GUI benchmarks [13].

The UI-Venus-2 framework has been developed as a general-purpose foundation GUI agent designed to operate across mobile, web, and desktop environments through a unified closed-loop reasoning-action framework [24]. It scales three critical dimensions: expanding environment coverage to more than 170 multilingual mobile apps and native desktop operating systems, employing a deep-research pipeline for function-grounded instruction generation, and adopting trace-level and sample-level evaluators to ensure reliable RL signals for training [24].

Additionally, research has been conducted on the robustness of GUI agents, with the introduction of AnTrap, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates agents against dynamic anomalies by injecting perturbations into agent execution trajectories [12]. This work reveals universal vulnerability to dynamic anomalies, with even the strongest models suffering significant performance degradation when encountering unexpected pop-ups or action misuse [12].

F03.question: Vad är det absolut  senaste inom Video genereation och är det hårdvaru- eller mjukvarurelaterat?
F03.answer:
The absolute latest in video generation is PhysStream [31], which introduces a physics-grounded video generation framework with structured scene memory and fine-grained motion control. PhysStream incorporates "structured scene memory" consisting of positional maps and object tracking maps derived from previously generated frames, and supports "fine-grained motion control via sparse velocity-increment signals that encode physical quantities, letting the model learn the underlying dynamics." [31]

This work represents a software-based advancement in video generation, as it describes a model and framework for physics-grounded image-to-video synthesis rather than a hardware solution. The approach enables "interactive, mid-generation control over multi-object tabletop rigid-body scenes," reducing motion distribution distance by 33% and trajectory error by 12% over previous baselines. [31]

No hardware-related solutions for video generation are mentioned in the most recent sources provided. All video generation advancements discussed in the latest papers (including PhysStream [31], Vidu S2 [26], and LynnReal-Omni [29]) are software-based frameworks or models.

F06.question: Vad är det senaste inom benchmarking av coding agents?
F06.answer:
The latest benchmark for coding agents mentioned in the sources is Real Suite [20]. According to the source, Real Suite "tests whether an AI can handle actual software engineering work" and involves tasks like "fixing invoice taxes or migrating customer accounts." It's described as having a "quite different design" compared to previous benchmarks, with the key challenge being "understanding how that particular company's software works, including rules scattered across different systems." A common failure mode is "simply missing a requirement," meaning "writing code is only part of the job, but the agent also has to figure out everything the change needs to accomplish." The leaderboard shows Fable 5.1 scoring 38.8% (number one), GPT6 Astra at 33.8%, and GLM 5.3 as the best open model at fourth place.

The source also notes that "software engineering benchmarks like Swebench or Deep Suite are already getting saturated very quickly," indicating Real Suite represents an emerging approach to address this saturation [20].

F07.question: Vad säger forskningen om text-to-video den senaste månaden?
F07.answer:
Research on text-to-video in the last month includes several key developments:

Temporal Context Routing (TCR) addresses a critical limitation in current joint audio-video generation models by aligning script timing with video and audio generation. TCR maps script timing onto the shared temporal axis and routes prompt guidance to corresponding positions, reducing Shot Boundary MAE by 96% (from 1.11s to 0.042s) and raising Dialogue Accuracy to 84.1% [23].

FIRM-Video introduces a reliable framework for text-to-video reward modeling using a "check-before-score" principle. It constructs dimension-specific checklists, verifies criteria against visual evidence, and aggregates only verified decisions to improve evaluation accuracy while addressing shortcomings in existing holistic judging approaches [30].

MiniMax has released a new video model capable of generating a 15-second video in just 13 seconds, enabling "infinite streams" where video generation continues faster than playback, allowing users to create continuous video content by prompting in real-time [27].

A survey on inference efficiency for VideoLLMs reveals that text-to-video generation remains computationally expensive, with models requiring substantial resources for high-quality output. The survey examines various efficiency mechanisms across frame sampling, modality encoding, and token reduction to address these challenges [31].

F08.question: Nämns LEGO i någon artikel och i så fall, sammanfatta vad de handlar om.
F08.answer: Yes, LEGO is mentioned in article [33]. LEGO-RL is a framework for harness-native reinforcement learning for coding agents that bridges native coding-agent harnesses with scalable policy-gradient optimization without modifying their internal control flow [33]. It is built upon three pillars: (1) faithful optimization via in-process LLM proxying for token-level alignment, (2) reliable execution through scalable sandbox orchestration to mitigate reward hacking, and (3) observable training with integrated validation and monitoring tools [33]. The framework was evaluated by training Qwen3.5-35B-A3B across three native coding-agent harnesses, improving performance on coding benchmarks like OpenHands SDK (64.0% to 70.4%), Claude Code (62.4% to 68.2%), and OpenCode (57.2% to 66.6%) while maintaining a high rollout-training probability correlation [33].

F15.question: Vad har hänt med AI-agenter den senaste veckan, i både papers och videor?
F15.answer:
Recent developments in AI agents span both academic research and practical applications, with key advancements in agent capabilities, safety, and real-world integration. [3] Introduces Occamy-1.0, a cost-efficient co-work model optimized for executing complex workflows across multiple tool invocations, achieving strong performance on benchmarks while maintaining low operational costs. [7] presents HazardAuditor, an execution-grounded framework improving safety for computer-use agents by normalizing interactions across heterogeneous agent frameworks and reducing safety errors by up to 16.5 percentage points. [11] demonstrates Agent as Policy (AGP), enabling general-purpose agents to directly control physical robots for tasks like block construction with success rates of 80-100% without task-specific training. [18] introduces RSIAgent, a training-free framework for autonomous exploration that recursively improves agent capabilities through memory construction, enabling open-source models to outperform frontier closed-source systems. [22] describes Atria Dawn Preview, a foundation agentic model trained via a Verifiable Experience Pipeline, achieving top scores on five real-world research benchmarks while highlighting human-AI collaboration dynamics. [25] reveals Emergence World, a multi-agent stress-testing environment showing that even individually safe agents can form systems with emergent failure modes, emphasizing the need for resilient system design over model-level alignment.  

In practical applications, [4] and [17] showcase GPT-6 Astra enabling AI software factories where agents autonomously build applications through GitHub issues, validated by pull requests.
